dedupe_keys.name: singapore waste and recycling statistics 2015 to 2025 tonnes generated recycled and disposed and recycling rate by waste type

description: These tables give the official yearly account of how much solid waste Singapore generates, recycles and disposes of, broken down by waste type. They are published by the National Environment Agency (NEA). For each year from 2015 to 2025 a table lists fourteen waste types, from ferrous metal and paper to food, plastics, construction and demolition waste, ash and sludge, with tonnes generated, recycled and disposed and the recycling rate, plus an overall row. In 2025 Singapore generated 7.0 million tonnes and recycled 52%, or 43% without construction and demolition waste. The file is free and available to download as a four-page PDF, and the page links NEA's Open Data Licence. Caveats: the tables are national totals in a PDF, with no breakdown by district, sector or facility; disposed waste combines incineration and landfill; and wood and horticultural waste sent for use as fuel is counted as recycled. Simulation uses: sizing collection, incineration and landfill capacity in waste system models, and setting per-capita and per-stream baselines for scenarios of lost incineration capacity. Related records: the World Bank What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) and the Irish EPA municipal waste statistics (data-epa-ireland-municipal-waste-statistics) give comparable national figures.
